correctness.rationale: The transformed ODE v’=kappa v(2-v), kappa’=epsilon(v-kappa) is exact on 0<v<2. Variation of constants bounds kappa and provides finite first upward crossing to fixed c. Independently simplified d[e^(-2kappa/epsilon)/v]/dt=-(2-kappa)e^(-2kappa/epsilon) in SymPy. Integrating logit gives int kappa=(1/2)log(c(2-v0)/(v0(2-c))); the quadratic-coupling balance gives int kappa^2=log((2-v0)/(2-c))+(kappa0^2-kappa(T)^2)/(2epsilon), uniformly bounded. Thus the Taylor remainder is integrable even as T grows, proving exactly the inverse-v0 and logarithmic coefficients; the angular rho^(-2) conversion follows from 1-cos rho=rho^2/2+O(rho^4). No uniformity in epsilon,c,kappa0 or global network assertion.
